sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation
Because no information is available on the use of nebivolol during breastfeeding, an alternate drug may be preferred, especially while nursing a newborn or preterm infant.
Drug Levels and Effects > Drug Levels

The excretion of beta-adrenergic blocking drugs into breastmilk is largely determined by their protein binding. Those with low binding are more extensively excreted into breastmilk. Accumulation of the drugs in the infant is related to the excretion rate. With 98% protein binding and a relatively long half-life, nebivolol presents a moderate risk for accumulation in infants.
